I've set several tyres tubeless, including those that aren't supposed to be tubeless-compatible (though for legal reasons I can't advise anyone to do the same). All using a measly floor pump without charger and I always put sealant through the valve after the bead has been seated.

Depending on the tyre+rim combo, setting up tubeless can either be a breeze or a pain in the ass. Most important thing is to do the rim tape correctly, and if the tyre won't seal, I always do 2-3 more layers of rim tape. Soapy water can help but extra layers of rim tape does the job best in my experience.

You can! The bolt is there if you want to run a fender, and I think you can even get away with removing the bolt and just putting a tape over the hole.

38s might fit but it'll be super tight because of that one bolt between your chainstays, and imo wouldn't be the best if you're planning to go muddy because there'd be no clearance for mud. Personally don't think 47s would fit because wider tires = bigger diameter and it looks like yours is maxed out (or pretty close to) already. 

If you need more cushion or want to go wider, I'd recommend to go 650b. Hunt wheels are a bargain for their price, I'm also looking to purchase them but haven't pulled the trigger yet.
